name: application-currency-input
title: Currency Input
description: Masked money field with a currency symbol prefix, thousands grouping in the displayed value, and a currency-code selector.
useWhen: Collecting a monetary amount such as a price, refund, or invoice line item.
The product supports more than one currency and the user needs to pick which one applies.
You want the symbol and currency code visually attached to the field rather than in a separate label.
avoidWhen: Only a single fixed currency is ever used and switching adds no value — drop the currency select and hardcode the symbol prefix.
You need full locale-aware parsing/formatting (grouping separators, decimal marks) — wire that with a library like Intl.NumberFormat and pass the formatted string in as `value`.
The value isn't actually money (e.g. a plain quantity) — use inputs or quantity-inputs instead.
responsiveBehavior: The field is a fixed max-w-xs block that fills its container's available width up to that cap at all breakpoints.
accessibility: The currency symbol is aria-hidden since it's redundant with the visible currency code in the adjacent select.
The currency <select> has a visually hidden but programmatically available label so screen readers announce its purpose.
The error message uses role="alert" and is linked via aria-describedby, with aria-invalid set on the input in the error state.

variants.title: Currency input
variants.description: Price field with a dollar-sign prefix, formatted amount, and a currency-code selector.
accessibility: Focus-within styling on the wrapper makes the whole control read as focused when either the input or select has focus.

variants.title: Currency input (Dark)
variants.description: Currency input adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Input, symbol, and select text colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.

variants.title: Error state
variants.description: Same field with a validation error: red border/ring and an alert message explaining the constraint that was violated.
accessibility: aria-invalid and aria-describedby are set together so the error is announced when the field receives focus.

variants.title: Error state (Dark)
variants.description: Currency input error state adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Error border and message colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
